Definition: from a reflexive pronoun otherwise obsolete and the genitive case (dative case or accusative case) of G846; him- (her-, it-, them-, also (in conjunction with the personal pronoun of the other persons) my-, thy-, our-, your-) self (selves), etc.:--alone, her (own, -self), (he) himself, his (own), itself, one (to) another, our (thine) own(-selves), + that she had, their (own, own selves), (of) them(-selves), they, thyself, you, your (own, own conceits, own selves, -selves).
BiblicalUsage: Heautou is the word for self, himself, herself, itself, and it is everywhere in the New Testament because the gospel is always personal. In Matthew 16:24 a man must deny himself and take up his cross, in 1 Corinthians 11:28 a man must examine himself before he eats, and in 2 Corinthians 13:5 Paul says examine yourselves whether ye be in the faith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word keeps the faith honest: denying self, examining self, proving self; the gospel is not about other people's sins, it starts with my own.
